[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Cloud Platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) with Python"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides an overview of using Python to interact with major cloud platforms: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). We'll cover basic setup, authentication, and common operations using Python SDKs."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"AWS with Python (Boto3)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Boto3 is the AWS SDK for Python. It allows you to manage AWS services like S3, EC2, and more. First, install Boto3:"},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install boto3"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Configure your AWS credentials. The easiest way is to configure the AWS CLI:"},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"aws configure"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"This will prompt you for your Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, region, and output format."},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here's an example of listing S3 buckets:"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import boto3

s3 = boto3.client('s3')
response = s3.list_buckets()

for bucket in response['Buckets']:
    print(f'Bucket Name: {bucket["Name"]} ')"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Azure with Python (Azure SDK for Python)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Azure SDK for Python allows you to interact with Azure services. Install the necessary packages. For example, to work with Azure Storage:"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"pip install azure-storage-blob"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"You'll need your Azure Storage account name and key. You can find these in the Azure portal."},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here's an example of listing blobs in a container:"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"from azure.storage.blob import BlobServiceClient

account_name = 'your_account_name'
account_key = 'your_account_key'
container_name = 'your_container_name'

connect_str = f'DefaultEndpointsProtocol=https;AccountName={account_name};AccountKey={account_key};EndpointSuffix=core.windows.net'

blob_service_client = BlobServiceClient.from_connection_string(connect_str)
container_client = blob_service_client.get_container_client(container_name)

blob_list = container_client.list_blobs()
for blob in blob_list:
    print(blob.name)"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"GCP with Python (Google Cloud Client Libraries)"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Google Cloud Client Libraries for Python provide access to GCP services. Install the relevant library. For example, to work with Google Cloud Storage:"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"pip install google-cloud-storage"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Authentication typically involves setting the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable to the path of your service account key file. You can download this file from the GCP Console."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/path/to/your/service-account-key.json""},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here's an example of listing buckets:"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"from google.cloud import storage

client = storage.Client()
buckets = client.list_buckets()

for bucket in buckets:
    print(bucket.name)"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Operations"},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Uploading Files: Each cloud provider has methods for uploading files to their respective storage services (S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage)."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Downloading Files: Similarly, you can download files from cloud storage using the SDKs."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Managing Compute Instances: You can start, stop, and manage virtual machines (EC2, Azure VMs, Compute Engine) programmatically."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Working with Databases: Interact with cloud-based databases like RDS, Azure SQL Database, and Cloud SQL."},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Error Handling"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cloud SDKs typically raise exceptions for errors. Wrap your code in try...except blocks to handle potential issues like network errors, permission problems, or invalid credentials."},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"try:
    # Cloud operation
    pass
except Exception as e:
    print(f"An error occurred: {e}")"},{"order":32,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":33,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a basic introduction to using Python with AWS, Azure, and GCP. Each cloud platform offers a wide range of services and features, so explore the SDK documentation for more advanced usage."}]
